A Key Management Appliance backed by a Hardware Security Module (per FIPS 140-2-L3). Only available in the ServiceNow Cloud.
A file-based Key Store that contains the Instance Root Key, and is securely stored on each application node.
A Root Key Wrapper is the highest level of protection in the envelope key wrapping design of ServiceNow's Key Management Framework.
The Instance Key Encryption Key (IKEK) wraps module keys to guarantee their confidentiality.
The Instance HMAC Key (IHMAC) signs module keys to guarantee their authenticity.
Instance Keys protect the confidentiality and authenticity of Module Keys used by applications and integrations. They are in turn protected by the Instance Root Key.
LDAP is a public key service that instances leverage when they exchange data within the ServiceNow Cloud.
The Asymmetric Key Encryption Key wraps keys exchanged between instances, for example during a Resource Exchange.
The Signing Key protects messages exchanged by ServiceNow instances when they communicate with each other, for example when one codesigns an update set before exporting it.
Vault is a public key service that instances leverage when they exchange data within the ServiceNow Cloud.
The Asymmetric Key Encryption Key wraps keys exchanged between instances, for example during a Resource Exchange.
The Signing Key protects messages exchanged by ServiceNow instances when they communicate with each other, for example when one codesigns an update before exporting it.
ServiceNow's internal Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) allows instances to securely communicate together by guaranteeing confidentiality and authenticity of the exchange.
The Instance Certificate Signing Key (ICSK) is used by ServiceNow's Key Management Framework to issue certificates.
The Issuing Certificate is the intermediate X.509 digital certificate that represents the identity of a ServiceNow instance in a chain of trust.
The CRL Endpoint advertises certificates that have been issued by an instance that are now revoked. It is per-instance, and managed by ServiceNow's Key Management Framework.
The Instance Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) component allows a ServiceNow instance to act as an issuer in a X.509 trust hierarchy.
GlideEncrypter is the backbone of the 2-Way Encrypted Password feature. It is backed by a parent cryptographic module that has dedicated child modules for each platform application.
Cryptographic modules are the centerpiece of ServiceNow's Key Management Framework. They define the specific mechanisms used for cryptographic operations given a specific use case.
